source: Numerics/Functions/LinearFunction.cs, PowerFunction.cs, TabularFunction.cs; Test_Numerics/Functions/Test_Functions.cs (Test_Linear_Function, Test_Linear_Function_Inverse, Test_Power_Function, Test_Power_Function_Inverse, Test_InversePower_Function, Test_InversePower_Function_Inverse, Test_Tabular_Function).
reference: Numerics @ 2a0357a. Every case whose "source" names a Test_Functions.cs method transcribes that method's own literal (or, for the two Test_*_Inverse round-trip methods, the intermediate Function() value computed by the SAME closed-form arithmetic the C# deterministic branch evaluates -- alpha + beta*x for linear, alpha*(x-xi)^beta for power -- since only the final round-trip identity, not the intermediate value, is a literal in the C# test). The two "*_confidence_inverse" cases exercise InverseFunction() under a set ConfidenceLevel, a combination Test_Functions.cs never asserts as a literal (it only asserts the Function()-then-InverseFunction() round trip recovers the original x, at ConfidenceLevel 0.75, for a DIFFERENT alpha/beta/sigma/xi than used here) -- curated via oracle_emitter --dump against the real C# LinearFunction/PowerFunction, per the fixtures/README.md bivariate_copula/multivariate_distribution curation convention. The four "tabular_*" cases (P4 Task 10) transcribe Test_Tabular_Function's own x = {50,100,150,200,250}, distributions = Deterministic(100,200,300,400,500), XTransform = Logarithmic, YTransform = None fixture -- Function(50) and InverseFunction(100) at the two boundary-clamp literals, and Function(75)/InverseFunction(Function(75)) at the intermediate closed-form value the C# test itself computes (100 + (200-100)/(ln(100)-ln(50))*(ln(75)-ln(50))) rather than asserting as its own separate literal.
